HON and GE. Honeywell and GE Aerospace.

His accounts bought more than $1.2 million of Honeywell and up to $3 million of GE Aerospace in 2025.

Part of a larger wave of defense purchases totaling at least $10 million that year.

GE Aerospace makes engines and components used across a wide range of military aircraft.

Honeywell provides aerospace systems, avionics, and defense technology supporting the same platforms.

Both sit deep in the supply chain for the planes the military relies on.

This lines up with the push for bigger defense budgets and the real-world operations involving Iran.

Aircraft from those campaigns needed parts and support, which fed into stockpile rebuilding and new contracts.

These companies benefit whenever military aviation gets prioritized.

These are bigger names than some of the smaller defense plays, but still less discussed than the pure-play contractors.

Everything is handled through independent managers with no direct input from him, as usual.

Still, the overlap with aerospace demand driven by his own spending policies is hard to miss.
